import html # Pre‑existing template string with placeholders for the post's components. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

Posted by: {writer_name}

{body}
{tags}
""" def generate_post_html(writer_name: str, title: str, body: str, tag_list: list[str]) -> str: """ Construct a safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- writer_name : str The name of the author. title : str The headline of the post. body : str The main content of the post. tag_list : list[str] A collection of tags related to the post. Returns ------- str An XSS‑protected HTML string representing the post. Raises ------ ValueError If any argument is not of an expected type. """ # Validate input types to avoid unexpected behavior if not isinstance(writer_name, str): raise ValueError("writer_name must be a string") if not isinstance(title, str): raise ValueError("title must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise ValueError("body must be a string") if not (isinstance(tag_list, list) and all(isinstance(t, str) for t in tag_list)): raise ValueError("tag_list must be a list of strings") # Escape all user‑supplied content to neutralize special HTML characters escaped_writer_name = html.escape(writer_name, quote=True) escaped_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) escaped_body = html.escape(body, quote=True) # Build the tags string: each tag inside a , escaped as well escaped_tags = "".join( f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in tag_list ) # Format the template with the escaped values return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( writer_name=escaped_writer_name, title=escaped_title, body=escaped_body, tags=escaped_tags )
